title: The Thirteenth Chime
hook: My new town had one rule: if the clock in the square ever strikes thirteen, turn off every light.
lines: The week I moved to Alder Falls, my neighbor told me the town's only rule.
If the clock in the square ever strikes thirteen... turn off every light, and stay away from the windows.
Two months later, the bells woke me just after midnight.
I counted in the dark. Eleven. Twelve.
Up and down the street, porch lights went out, one by one. All except mine.
Through the gap in the curtains, I saw them. Tall gray shapes, walking slowly down the middle of the road.
I hit the switch so hard it cracked, and I sat on the floor until sunrise.
In the morning, my neighbor was waiting at the fence, pale as paper.
A lit porch is an invitation, she whispered. But you turned it off in time.
Then she looked past me, through my kitchen window... and asked who was making breakfast.
